verdicts.title: The only in-repo performance gate is fail-open: a kernel 20% slower at equal memory asserts 'benefit'
verdicts.reasoning: Assertion logic verified verbatim at packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels/conftest.py:164-178: speedup = pt_time/op_time, mem_reduction = pt_mem/op_mem, has_benefit = speedup > (1.0 - max_perf_overhead) or mem_reduction > 1.0, default max_perf_overhead=0.20. A kernel 1.20x slower (speedup 0.833) at unchanged peak memory (mem_reduction == 1.0, which fails the memory arm) still satisfies the speed arm and passes. 90 call sites across 10 kernel test files; several widen the tolerance further (0.30 in test_geglu.py:310,594; 0.50 in test_lora.py:570,1569; 0.60 in test_cross_entropy.py:497). No benchmarks/ directory; none of the 15 .github/workflows files is performance-related. TWO EVIDENCE ITEMS ARE WRONG and I corrected them: (1) the harness DOES have an artifact path - conftest.py:219-296 adds a --record-perf=PATH pytest option and pytest_sessionfinish flushes one JSON row per assert_perf_benefit call carrying nodeid, label, torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), both times, both memories, speedup and mem_reduction; what is true is that no workflow passes --record-perf (grep for 'record-perf' across .github/ returns nothing) and no baseline is committed, so the facility is unused; (2) 'every consumer is CUDA-marked' is wrong for test_linear_cross_entropy.py:38 and test_lora.py:44, which are skipif-only with no pytest.mark.cuda - so those files are skipped on CPU lanes AND excluded from the -m "cuda" CUDA lanes, which is exactly open issue #880. The remaining files (test_rope, test_rms_norm, test_swiglu, test_cross_entropy, test_geglu, test_fused_add_rms_norm) carry [pytest.mark.cuda, skipif]. So the gate never runs on Linux amd64 / macOS arm64 / Linux arm64 / dependency-boundary lanes, as claimed. Downgraded in substance: the tolerance is an explicit, documented, per-call-site parameter and the docstring states the intent ('benefit in speed or memory'), so this is a permissive-by-design gate with no baseline rather than an accidental fail-open; it has zero runtime, numerical or privacy effect. The substance (no committed baseline, no harness, no recorded reference point) is the content of open #417, which the finding itself proposes folding it into.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A fused-kernel change regresses wall time by up to 20% (or up to 30/50/60% at the call sites that widen max_perf_overhead) without increasing peak CUDA memory. _assert_perf_benefit still passes because the speed arm only fails below 0.8x, and the memory arm is a disjunct. The measurement is printed to captured stdout; a machine-readable row is produced only if the run passes --record-perf=PATH, which no CI workflow does, and there is no committed baseline to compare against. On top of that the whole gate is CUDA-only, so no PR or main lane other than the self-hosted CUDA lanes evaluates it at all (and test_linear_cross_entropy.py / test_lora.py, being skipif-only with no cuda marker, are not selected even there - open #880). Consequence is limited to undetected performance drift; no correctness or privacy impact.

verdicts.title: calibrate()'s runtime-unsafe fallback drops the adaptive-probe union bound but still reports the undivided mc_failure_probability
verdicts.reasoning: Code path verified in packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/calibration.py: line 303 probe_count = max_iterations + 2; 304-309 probe_config divides mc_failure_probability by probe_count; 310-317 the primary search runs under probe_config; 320-330 the calibrated parameter is re-evaluated once, non-adaptively, under overall_config (this single evaluation is what legitimises reporting the undivided value on the primary path); 331-341 when runtime_safe is False the ENTIRE binary search is re-run by _calibrate_impl while still inside `with _use_discretization(overall_config)`, so every probe of that second search consumes the full mc_failure_probability, and `achieved = result.achieved` takes the reported value straight from an adaptively selected probe of that search with no non-adaptive re-evaluation; line 353 then sets result.mc_failure_probability = overall_config.mc_failure_probability. That contradicts the documented contract at calibration.py:79-81 ('Overall failure probability covering every adaptive Monte Carlo probe'). REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY TWICE by wrapping _calibrate_impl: (a) mc_resolution=1e-2, balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(nm, blt_strategy()), num_bins=5, n_steps=20), epsilon_budget(8.0, 1e-5), param range 0.5-8.0 -> invocations=2, second invocation at mc_failure_probability=1e-06 with 19 iterations, reported mc_failure_probability=1e-06; (b) the SAME call at the library's true defaults (mc_resolution=1e-5, mc_failure_probability=1e-6, 2,940,252 MC samples) -> invocations=2 again, second search at 1e-06 with 19 iterations, reported 1e-06. So the fallback is reachable with default discretization and default tolerance, not only in a corner case. (A smaller case, num_bins=2/n_steps=4 at defaults, did NOT trigger it - invocations=1 - so it is config-dependent, not universal.) MAGNITUDE, which the finding overstates: the honest union over ~21 probes is ~2.1e-5 rather than 1e-6, i.e. the reported confidence is optimistic by ~21x in a quantity of order 1e-5. Because resolved_num_mc_samples is itself derived from mc_failure_probability, re-evaluating the same converged process at 1e-6/22 vs 1e-6 vs 2.2e-5 gave epsilon 7.98944 / 7.99999 / 8.01978 - under 0.3% spread - and at default mc_resolution the value was insensitive. So the defect is a mislabelled confidence field, not a materially understated epsilon. Existing tests do not catch it: test_calibration_reports_one_overall_mc_confidence_budget (packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_b_min_sep.py:229) asserts exactly the reported-equals-configured behaviour, and test_recalibrates_when_runtime_evaluation_is_unsafe (packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_calibration.py:608) only pins that the fallback produces a safe `achieved`. No open tracked issue covers this (#911 is about MC calibration performance).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With default discretization (mc_resolution=1e-5, mc_failure_probability=1e-6) a user calls cal.calibrate(cal.epsilon_budget(8.0, delta=1e-5), lambda nm: balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(nm, blt_strategy()), num_bins=5, n_steps=20), 0.5, 8.0). The probe-config search converges, the single runtime re-evaluation at that parameter lands above the budget, so runtime_safe is False and calibrate() re-runs the whole binary search inside `with _use_discretization(overall_config)`: 19 iterations / ~21 Monte Carlo probes, each consuming the undivided 1e-6 rather than 1e-6/102, and the returned `achieved` is taken from one adaptively selected probe of that search. CalibrateResult.mc_failure_probability is nevertheless reported as 1e-06 (mc_confidence 0.999999), although the simultaneous coverage of those probes is only about 1-2.1e-5 - a failure mass larger than the delta=1e-5 the user calibrated at. Measured impact on the number itself is small: correcting the per-probe bound to 1e-6/22 changes the achieved epsilon by under 0.3% (7.98944 vs 7.99999 at mc_resolution=1e-2) and was not measurable at default mc_resolution. So the concrete defect is a documented confidence field that is optimistic by roughly the probe count on a path reachable at defaults, not a materially wrong epsilon.

verdicts.title: b-min-sep Monte Carlo transcript reuse is silently inert at default settings for any horizon above 60 steps
verdicts.reasoning: Verified end to end. packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_b_min_sep/_transcript_cache.py:13-20 sizes the corpus as nbytes_estimate = 3 * num_mc_samples * n_steps * 8 against default_max_bytes = 4 GiB (env OPAQUE_B_MIN_SEP_TRANSCRIPT_CACHE_MAX_BYTES). The estimate is exact, not a guess: packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:209-211 allocates three Vec<f64> of num_samples*n_steps cells (remove_x, remove_zeta, add_eta) held by BMinSepTranscriptCorpus (registry.rs:17-24). Measured with the installed build: DiscretizationConfig().resolved_num_mc_samples == 2,940,252 at defaults; 3*2940252*8 = 70.6 MB per step; the largest horizon that fits 4 GiB is n_steps = 60; and tc.with_handle((1.0,0.0), 100, 0.001, 2940252, 42, <raises-if-called>) returned None WITHOUT invoking the factory - i.e. at n_steps=100 the reuse path is refused before any work. BMinSep.pld (_b_min_sep/__init__.py:182-203) then falls through to _native.bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld for every probe, with no warning: config.warn_if_large_mc() warns only about the sample count, never about the rejected corpus. MECHANISM CORRECTION: NativeCache.with_handle (packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_native_cache.py:105-127) returns None directly when nbytes > max_bytes; it does not raise, so the `except ValueError: return None` in _transcript_cache.py:90-94 is vestigial. Outcome is identical. The existing tests (packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_b_min_sep.py:73-190) only exercise 64-80 sample corpora, so none of them reaches the default-size case. Severity lowered from medium to low: this is performance only (affects_epsilon false, no numerical change - the fallback computes the same PLD), the reuse path is inherently memory-bound by design rather than mis-budgeted (even n_steps=60 needs ~3.9 GiB of resident f64), and the substance - b-min-sep MC calibration being impractically slow - is open tracked issue #911, which the finding itself says it belongs to. I did not independently time the with-reuse vs without-reuse calibration, so the size of the lost speedup is unquantified here.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: At default discretization (2,940,252 MC samples) any b_min_sep(...) with n_steps > 60 requests a transcript corpus larger than the 4 GiB cap (6.57 GiB at n_steps=100, 65.7 GiB at 1000, 131 GiB at 2000). NativeCache.with_handle returns None before creating anything, _transcript_cache.with_handle passes the None through, and BMinSep.pld silently recomputes the full warm-start Monte Carlo via bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld for every calibration probe. Nothing warns, nothing names the estimated bytes or the cap, and raising the env cap to the required tens or hundreds of GiB is not a real option, so the sigma-independent reuse optimisation is unreachable at every realistic DP-FTRL horizon while still being exercised by tests only at 64-80 samples. Impact is calibration wall time; the computed PLD and epsilon are unchanged.

verdicts.title: The GQA de-replication fix (#985) multiplies SDPA dispatch count by num_key_value_heads on every vmapped attention path
verdicts.reasoning: Every structural link verified in packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py at the current tree: _grouped_sdpa (line 75) short-circuits to one SDPA when num_key_value_groups == 1 (82-91) and otherwise loops `for key_value_head in range(key.shape[-3])` (97) issuing one scaled_dot_product_attention per KV head over expanded (stride-0, no-copy) _kv_group views (64-72); _can_use_native_gqa (116-121) returns False for any device that is not CUDA and for any torch._C._functorch.is_batchedtensor(query), so under the DP vmap the loop is always taken for GQA; _compact_sliding_window_sdpa (244-274) wraps it in a fixed 64-query chunk loop (_SDPA_QUERY_CHUNK = 64 at line 10); the Gemma2 softcap forward (514-545) and backward (584+) carry the same nested chunk x KV-head loops. git show b9fb8674^ confirms the pre-#985 form did vmap_repeat_kv once and a single SDPA per chunk. MEASURED MYSELF on the current tree: vmap(grad(...)) through vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window at S=1024, window=256, 8 query / 2 KV heads issues exactly 32 scaled_dot_product_attention calls per layer = ceil(1024/64) * 2, versus 16 for the same shape with num_key_value_groups == 1. Also verified on torch 2.14.0+cu130 that FuncTorchBatched kernels exist for aten::_scaled_dot_product_{flash,efficient,cudnn}_attention but for NONE of their _backward variants (nor for the CPU flash variants), so backward falls out to the per-example batched fallback and the dispatch count multiplies again there. Mistral and Ministral do register this path (models/mistral.py:32, models/ministral.py:32). WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: no GPU was available, so the claim that throughput 'becomes launch-bound' at S=8192 / 32 layers is arithmetic extrapolation, not measurement; the 1024-calls-per-layer figure assumes Mistral-7B geometry (8 KV heads) and that the compact path is entered (it needs attention_mask None, position_bias None, dropout 0 and seq > sliding_window). As a proxy I timed old-vs-new under vmap(grad) on CPU at S=1024/QH=8/KVH=2: 0.089 s vs 0.118 s per iteration, i.e. the looped form is ~1.33x slower in wall time there while avoiding the vmap_repeat_kv reshape copy. Severity lowered from medium to low: it is a deliberate memory-for-launches trade (the memory win is real), affects no numerical or privacy behaviour, and the per-layer loop count claim is the only part I could measure. Also note a small imprecision in the finding: the Gemma2 softcap loops dispatch matmul/softmax, not SDPA, so they do not add to the 'SDPA dispatch count'. The substance sits inside open #963 (tune compact sliding-window attention) and #958 (batch fused SDPA across the DP vmap dimension), as the finding itself states.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Since b9fb8674 (#985), any GQA model under the DP vmap takes the _grouped_sdpa loop, because _can_use_native_gqa refuses batched tensors. Composed with the fixed 64-query chunk loop of _compact_sliding_window_sdpa, one Mistral/Ministral attention layer issues ceil(seq/64) * num_key_value_heads scaled_dot_product_attention calls in forward instead of ceil(seq/64) - measured as exactly 32 calls at seq=1024, window=256, 8 query / 2 KV heads, against 16 for the MHA shape. Because torch 2.14 has no functorch batching rule for any SDPA backward op, the backward pass fans each of those out again per physical microbatch example. Extrapolating the same structure to Mistral-7B geometry at seq=8192 / window=4096 gives 128 chunks x 8 KV heads = 1024 forward SDPA calls per layer. On CPU under vmap(grad) the looped form measured ~1.33x slower than the pre-#985 vmap_repeat_kv form at S=1024/QH=8/KVH=2; the corresponding GPU throughput cost was not measured here, and the change does buy a real reduction in K/V materialisation.
